title: Schema-first streaming adapters with incremental validation and retry-safety for Python SDK
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Background:
We have multiple customer requests and internal PRs showing confusion when consuming streaming responses and trying to hydrate typed models incrementally. Current SDK helpers encourage fully buffering or naive chunk-to-json assembly which causes: broken partial validation, awkward user code to handle backpressure, and lost idempotency safety when retries re-stream responses.

Problem statement:
- Provide a schema-first streaming API for the Python SDK that:
  * Accepts Pydantic models and dataclasses as the canonical contract for each streamed message
  * Validates incrementally so users can act on partial but well-formed fragments (e.g., partial embeddings, token-level metadata) without buffering the entire response
  * Is retry-safe: when the SDK retries a request (e.g., transient network), applications can deduplicate or resume without producing duplicate side effects (webhook delivery, DB writes)
  * Plays nicely with backpressure and async iterators so users can pause/resume consumption

Design proposal (high level):
1) API surface: add a new helper `stream_as(schema, on_chunk=None, validate_incrementally=True, idempotency_key=None)` available in both sync and async variants. Example usage: 

```python
from typing import AsyncIterator
from pydantic import BaseModel
from redwood_sdk import Client

class TokenDelta(BaseModel):
    token: str
    finished: bool = False

client = Client()

async def handle_stream():
    async for chunk in client.stream_as(schema=TokenDelta, idempotency_key="user:chat:123"):
        # chunk is a TokenDelta instance (partial or complete depending on schema)
        if chunk.token:
            await websocket.send(chunk.token)
        if chunk.finished:
            break
```

2) Incremental parsing behavior:
- The SDK will parse incremental JSON fragments into model instances where possible.
- When `validate_incrementally=True`, the parser will attempt partial validation and attach a `_partial` attribute on the model instance (string flag) for fields that are still incomplete.
- A user can opt into strict behavior (`validate_incrementally=False`) to only yield fully validated models.

3) Retry-safety and idempotency:
- The SDK accepts an `idempotency_key` parameter and will send it to the backend as a header.
- For client-side retries where the backend cannot deduplicate the streamed side effects, the SDK exposes a `resume_token` mechanism emitted as part of the stream metadata. Applications can persist resume tokens alongside their idempotency key.
- When resuming, the SDK will request the stream starting from `resume_token` and drop messages up to that token locally.

4) Backpressure and flow control:
- The returned object implements Python async iterator protocol and exposes a `.pause()` / `.resume()` pair for manual flow control (useful for websockets or downstream slow consumers).
- Additionally, it exposes a `max_buffer_size` config and will apply backpressure by requesting the server to slow token emission via the transport when supported.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Pydantic vs dataclasses: support both by internal adapter layers. Pydantic models get strict runtime validation; dataclasses use our lightweight runtime coercion util (faster but less strict).
- Partial instances: adding `_partial` metadata breaks pure typing but is acceptable as an opt-in ergonomic feature documented thoroughly.
- Resume_token reliance on backend: requires runtime to emit stable resume tokens. We'll provide a fallback (idempotent client-side dedupe) but will prioritize server integration with the backend team (depend on ENG-23214).
- Streaming JSON formats: support both NDJSON per-line and SSE-like chunked envelopes. The parsing layer will be robust to occasional non-JSON control frames.

API sketch (detailed):
- client.stream_as(schema=ModelClass, *, validate_incrementally=True, idempotency_key=None, max_buffer_size=32, resume_from=None) -> AsyncIterator[ModelClass]
- Sync variant: client.stream_as_sync(...) -> Iterator[ModelClass]
- Stream object methods: .pause(), .resume(), .close(), .get_resume_token() -> Optional[str]

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Malformed chunk mid-model: emit a ValidationError model entry with `.error` field and continue (configurable to stop).
- Backpressure unsupported by transport: fall back to client drop-buffer or signal to user via warning label.
- Long-lived streams and memory: default max_buffer_size prevents unbounded growth; recommend user to persist resume tokens for long sessions.

Acceptance criteria (how we know it's done):
- SDK exposes the new `stream_as` API in async and sync flavors with documented examples.
- Provides compatibility with Pydantic BaseModel and dataclasses.
- Emits resume tokens and accepts resume_from for at-least-once safety; integration test with mocked backend shows dedupe/resume path.
- Backpressure primitives `.pause()`/`.resume()` implemented and exercised in example app (websocket relay).
- API docs and a short cookbook: "migrate from naive chunking to stream_as" included in docs site.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for incremental parsing with many corner cases (split tokens, multi-line ndjson, control frames).
- Integration test: fixture server that emits predictable tokens and resume tokens; assert resume+idempotency semantics.
- Load test: ensure default buffer prevents OOM when consumer is slow.
- Fuzz test: random chunk boundaries and syntactic noise.

Migration and rollout:
- Soft launch in 0.9.0: feature gated as `stream_as` in beta.
- Add telemetry for adoption and errors reported.
- Rich docs + example repository `redwood-examples/python/streaming-schema-first` with two demos: websocket relay and persistent job processor.

Dependencies and open items:
- Backend work to support resume tokens and idempotency header (blocker for full resume; partial paths implemented) - dependency ENG-23214.
- Confirm expected runtime formats and SSE control frames with infra (ENG-27841).
- UX review for `.pause()`/`.resume()` surface; coordinate with Docs/Developer DX.

Notes and links:
- Design doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/stream-as-design (WIP)
- PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1201 (prototype incremental parser)
- Example app: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/tree/main/python/streaming-schema-first

Timeline and milestones (rough):
- Week 1 (2026-02-20 -> 2026-02-26): prototype incremental parser and pydantic adapter (complete).
- Week 2 (2026-02-27 -> 2026-03-05): add resume_token plumbing, implement pause/resume primitives (in progress).
- Week 3 (2026-03-06 -> 2026-03-12): tests, integration with mocked backend, docs draft (blocked briefly on ENG-23214).
- Week 4 (2026-03-13 -> 2026-03-19): polish, examples, beta release under feature flag.

Open comments and review log:
- 2026-02-24 Marco Chen: initial prototype looks good; prefer `validate_incrementally` default true for streaming use-cases. Action: add explicit opt-out for strict consumers.
- 2026-03-02 Sofia Ramirez (Docs): request clearer examples for dataclasses interop and a migration note for existing `stream_text` users.
- 2026-03-06 Security (J. Liu): flagged potential info leak via resume_token stored in logs; need to ensure tokens are short-lived and marked PII (follow up).
- 2026-03-09 Aisha Patel: added example code and acceptance criteria; assigned to Marco for implementation and code review.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- Add telemetry for: validation-error rates, partial-yield ratio, resume_token usage.
- Create a short migration guide and record a 30-min internal demo.

Sidenote: This ticket intentionally focuses on ergonomics and safety rather than introducing new runtime transports. If the runtime needs protocol work, we'll spin a separate infra ticket and keep this SDK work backward-compatible.
